ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A particle moves through the first quadrant as follows. During the first minute it moves from the origin to $(1,0)$. Thereafter, it continues to follow the directions indicated in the figure, going back and forth between the positive $x$ and $y$ axes, moving one unit of distance parallel to an axis in each minute. At which point will the particle be after exactly $1989$ minutes?

The path starts from the origin, first goes along the x-axis to (1,0), then up to (1,1), left to (0,1), up to (0,2), right to (2,2), down to (2,0), right to (3,0), up to (3,3), left to (0,3), then up to (0,4), and continues to move according to this square broken-line path that expands back and forth between the positive x-axis and positive y-axis. Each unit length takes 1 minute.

Reasoning: From the first few segments in the figure, it can be seen that there is a pattern at square-number times: at t=1=1^2 it is at (1,0); at t=4=2^2 it is at (0,2); at t=9=3^2 it is at (3,0). Therefore in general, at t=n^2, if n is odd, the position is (n,0); if n is even, the position is (0,n). Because 44^2=1936, 45^2=2025, and 1989 is between the two, first look at t=1936. 44 is even, so at t=1936 the particle is at (0,44). Starting from such an even y-axis endpoint, the path shown next first goes right along the horizontal line y=44 for 44 minutes, reaching (44,44), and at this time the time is 1936+44=1980. There remain 1989-1980=9 minutes, then it goes down along x=44 for 9 units, so the y-coordinate is 44-9=35. Therefore the position is (44,35).
